# Ascribe's surface

Everything a person or an agent touches, read from where the code declares it. It says what exists, not whether it should: a plan that adds a command, a setting, a tool, or a diagnostic reads it to see what it's adding to, and its pull request's diff of this file shows what it added.

## The command line

For people and agents. Read from `docs/content/_generated/cli-synopsis.md`, `docs/content/_generated/cli-global-options.md`, `docs/content/reference/cli.md`.

| Command | What it's for | Arguments and options | `--format` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ascribe agents sync` | Writes `AGENTS.md` beside `ascribe.toml`, a short block in the repository root's `AGENTS.md` when the project is in a subfolder, and the skill in the root's `.agents/skills/ascribe/`. | `[--check] [--target agents-md\|skills\|claude\|claude-rules\|copilot\|codex]... [--with-hook] [--cloud] [--agent]` |  |
| `ascribe agents rules` | Prints your project's rules: the block `sync` writes into the `AGENTS.md` beside `ascribe.toml`, as it would write it now. | `[PATH]` |  |
| `ascribe agents skill` | Prints a file of the Ascribe skill, the same for every project: its `SKILL.md`, or its directive reference, `references/directives.md`. | `[FILE]` |  |
| `ascribe agents prompt` | Prints a named prompt for an agent, in the same form as Prompt agent's. | `[NAME] [--arg <KEY=VALUE>]... [--list]` |  |
| `ascribe agents hook` | Checks an agent's work as its hook runs it: after the agent writes a file, or before it finishes. | `HARNESS [--event edit\|stop]` |  |
| `ascribe build` | Checks the project, then writes each build's outputs. | `[--build <NAME>]... [--emit site,plain,json] [--anchors]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe check` | Checks every source file for problems, without building anything: every file-level diagnostic, then the page-level ones for **every build** in `ascribe.toml`. | `[PATHS]... [--stdin] [--path <PATH>] [--build <NAME>]... [--editor-build] [--summary] [--deny-warnings] [--fix] [--vale]` | `text`, `concise`, `json`, `prompt` |
| `ascribe diff` | Shows what changed between a git revision and the working tree, as readers will see it: which pages of each build changed, and which blocks on them were added, removed, changed, or moved. | `[PAGE] [--base <REV>] [--base-exact] [--build <NAME>]... [--exit-code] [--pages-only]` | `text`, `json`, `html`, `prompt` |
| `ascribe drift` | Lists the pages whose code examples changed between a git revision and the working tree, and whether the words around them changed too, and the pages whose examples no longer resolve. | `[--base <REV>] [--build <NAME>]... [--exit-code]` | `text`, `json`, `summary` |
| `ascribe explain` | Says what a diagnostic means: its severity, its messages, how to fix it, a link to its entry in Diagnostics, and, for the diagnostics people meet most, a short page that has the problem and the same page without it. | `[CODE] [--list]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe fmt` | Rewrites Ascribe constructs into canonical form: the spacing of directive lines and attribute blocks, attribute order, quoting, and blank lines between directives and their blocks. | `[--check] [PATHS]...` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe link` | Says whether a link works, written on a given page: whether its target exists, the page's title or the heading's text, and the destination to write there. | `TARGET --from <PAGE>` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe lsp` | Runs the language server, speaking the Language Server Protocol over standard input and output. |  |  |
| `ascribe mcp` | Runs an MCP server, speaking the Model Context Protocol over standard input and output, for an agent that has no shell, or a host that approves tools one by one. |  |  |
| `ascribe model` | Shows the content model as `ascribe` reads it, with the defaults filled in: page types with their files and frontmatter fields, dimensions, phrases, features, glossary terms, project widgets, builds, and sources with their folders and the files they make readable. | `[PATH] [--section types\|dimensions\|phrases\|features\|glossary\|widgets\|builds\|sources]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe outline` | Shows a page's title and type, and the headings a link to it can name, with the ids links write after `#`: the page's own headings and those that come from the fragments it includes. | `PAGE [--build <NAME>]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe permalinks sync` | Brings `ascribe.permalinks` up to date with the project, and makes it when there's none: it adds each permalink the list doesn't have, records where each is declared now, so moving a heading to another page and running `sync` changes one line, and records each alias and retired permalink as `ascribe.toml` has it. |  | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe permalinks list` | Shows every permalink the content declares, with the file and line it's declared on, and each alias and retired permalink in `ascribe.toml`, and says which ones `ascribe.permalinks` doesn't have yet, has somewhere else, or has that the project no longer has. |  | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe permalinks verify` | Checks that each name is a permalink or an alias in a list, and names each one that isn't, and each one that was retired, with the reason the docs give. | `[NAME]... [--from <FILE>] [--list <PATH>]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe permalinks retire` | Retires permalinks on purpose, with a reason: it writes an entry for each in `ascribe.toml`'s [`[permalinks.retired]`](content-model.md#20-permalinks), in place, keeping the file's comments and order, and, when the project has `ascribe.permalinks`, records there each one the content no longer declares. | `[NAME]... --reason <TEXT> [--to <PAGE>] [--page <PAGE>] [--under <FOLDER>]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe refs` | Lists the places that use a page, a fragment, a heading, or an entry of the content model, each as `file:line:column`, with what kind of use it is. | `TARGET [--limit <N>]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe rename` | Renames a phrase, a dimension's value, a heading's id, or a page, and changes everything that uses it, as the editor's rename does: it makes the same edits. | `TARGET NEW` |  |
| `ascribe render` | Writes a page as a reader of one build sees it: the plain Markdown the build's `plain` output writes for it, with its variants chosen, the blocks the build filters out removed, phrases and includes filled in, and links written as that output writes them. | `PAGE [--build <NAME>] [--frontmatter]` | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe report` | Reports what state a project is in, section by section: what's too slow, needs the network, or is too broad for `ascribe check`. | `[SECTION]... [--build <NAME>]... [--site <URL>] [--limit <N>] [--exit-code advice\|warning\|error]` | `text`, `summary`, `json`, `prompt` |
| `ascribe sources fetch` | Makes the copies match `ascribe.lock`: at each source's pin, it copies the files snippets name that have no copy or a wrong one, and removes the copies no snippet names. | `[NAME]...` |  |
| `ascribe sources update` | Moves each source's pin to the head of its `branch` (or to `--to`), copies the files snippets use again at the new commit, rewrites `ascribe.lock`, and says what changed: the commits between the old pin and the new (how many, and the first lines of the newest 20, or that the pin moved back), the copies that changed, and the pages whose examples changed, grouped as `ascribe drift` groups them. | `[NAME]... [--to <REV>]` | `text`, `json`, `summary` |
| `ascribe sources status` | Shows each source in another repository: its repository and branch, its pin, and each copy's state (current, changed here, missing, not in the lock, unused, not copied yet, or not in the repository at the pin). |  | `text`, `json` |
| `ascribe vale eject` | Writes the preset `[checks.vale]` names out as the project's own Vale configuration, for a project that wants more than turning a preset's rules off: `.vale.ini` and a `.vale/` styles folder at the project root, with the rules `off` names turned off in `.vale.ini`. |  |  |

On every command:

| Option | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `--config <PATH>` | The content model, `ascribe.toml`, or a directory that holds one. |
| `--color <WHEN>` | When to color text output. |

| `@include` | SPEC §4.2 |

## `ascribe.toml`

For authors. Read from `docs/content/reference/content-model.md`.

| Section | What it's for | In the reference |
|---|---|---|
| Top level: `spec` | The only other top-level keys are the tables in §3–§19. | §2 |
| `[project]` | Where the source lives and where builds write. | §3 |
| `[types.<name>]` and `[fragments]` | A **content type** is a frontmatter schema for a kind of page, plus the files it applies to. | §4 |
| `[dimensions.<name>]` | A **dimension** is an axis content varies along (SPEC §4.3), and whose values are availability targets (SPEC §4.4). | §6 |
| `[versions]` | How versions in availability specs are compared (SPEC §4.4), and which release is current. | §7 |
| `[lifecycle.<state>]` | Lifecycle states (SPEC §4.4). | §8 |
| `[features.<key>]` | The features registry (SPEC §4.4): named availability specs, so a feature going generally available takes one edit. | §9 |
| `[notes.<type>]` | Note types (SPEC §4.5), the values of `@note`'s `type` attribute. | §10 |
| `[phrases]` | The phrases registry (SPEC §5.1). | §11 |
| `[glossary]` | The glossary (SPEC §5.4): terms, their definitions, and how occurrences are matched. | §12 |
| `[images]` | Image attributes (SPEC §5.3): which keys may appear in an attribute block after an image, and their types. | §13 |
| `[widgets.<name>]` | Project widgets (SPEC §6): directives a documentation set defines. | §14 |
| `[consumer]` | The consumer profile (SPEC §9.5): how the site output fits a specific consumer. | §15 |
| `[builds.<name>]` | Named builds (SPEC §9.3). | §16 |
| `[editor]` | Settings for the authoring environment (SPEC §10). | §17 |
| `[sources.<name>]` | A source is a folder outside the project's content, or another repository, that its pages may take code examples from, with `@snippet` (SPEC §7.3). | §18 |
| `[checks]` | How loudly each check about your content's quality speaks: whether it's reported as advice, a warning, or an error, or not at all. | §19 |
| `[permalinks]` | Names for something outside the docs to link to that no heading or page declares: a permalink ended on purpose, and a second name for one. | §20 |

Actions, which the actions bar and the lightbulb offer where each applies:

| Action | What it does | Where it applies |
|---|---|---|
| Wrap in a note | Put the paragraph or the selected blocks in an `@note` callout. | A paragraph, or whole blocks selected |
| Change the note's kind | Set the `type` of the `@note` the cursor is in. | A note |
| Remove the note, keeping its text | Take the content out of its `@note`. | A note |
| Turn the note into collapsible details | Make the `@note` a `@details` block, with a title. | A note |
| Wrap in collapsible details | Put the block or the selected blocks in `@details`, with a title. | A paragraph, code block, table, include, or snippet, or whole blocks selected |
| Remove the details, keeping the content | Take the content out of its `@details` and its title. | A details block |
| Make the list steps | Show the numbered list as `@steps`. | A numbered list that isn't steps |
| Make the steps a plain list | Remove the list's `@steps`. | Steps |
| Give the heading a stable id | Add `@id:` under the heading, so links to it survive rewording it. | A heading without `@id` |
| Copy a link to this section | Copy the heading's destination from the content root, such as `/guides/install.md#install-cli`, to paste in any page. | A heading |
| Insert a note | Add an `@note` callout, with its text ready to type. | A blank line between blocks |
| Insert steps | Add `@steps` and a numbered list. | A blank line between blocks |
| Insert collapsible details | Add a `@details` block with a title. | A blank line between blocks |
| Insert content that varies | Add `@variant` arms, one for each value of a dimension you choose. | A blank line between blocks |
| Add a variant | Add a `@variant` arm for another value of the group's dimension. | A group of one dimension's `@variant` arms |
| Remove this variant | Remove the `@variant` arm the cursor is in from its group. | An arm of a group with others |
| Mark where it's available | Add `@available:` to the section or block, or `{available=…}` to the table row, with a feature or a spec. | A heading (its section), a block, or a table's body row |
| Make the page one variant | Set a dimension's value under `variant:` in the page's frontmatter. | Anywhere in a page |
| Set where the page is available | Set `available:` in the page's frontmatter, with a feature or a spec. | Anywhere in a page |
| Link the selected text | Make the selection a link, `text`, to a page or heading you choose. | Text selected in one paragraph or heading |
| Insert a link | Add a link, ``, to a page or heading you choose, that shows its title. | The cursor in a paragraph or heading, outside links and phrases |
| Change where the link goes | Set the link's destination to a page or heading you choose. | A link |
| Show the page's title as the link text | Empty the link's text, ``, so it shows its target's title. | A link to a page, with text |
| Insert a phrase | Add a phrase the content model declares, `{key}`, which shows its value. | The cursor in a paragraph or heading, outside links and phrases |
| Insert an image | Add an image of the project, `!alt`, with its alt text. | A blank line between blocks |
| Set the image's width | Set the image's `width` attribute. | An image |
| Change the image's description | Set the image's alt text, `![alt]`, which readers who can't see it get. | An image |
| Include a fragment | Add `@include:` for a fragment, a page, or one of its sections. | A blank line between blocks |
| Insert a code snippet | Add `@snippet:` with code from one of the project's sources. | A blank line between blocks |
| Insert a widget | Add one of the project's widgets, `@name`, with the attributes it needs. | A blank line between blocks |
| Make this a phrase | Declare the selected text in `[phrases]` and write `{key}` in its place, and in its other occurrences if you choose. | Text selected in one paragraph or heading |
| Add to the glossary | Declare the selected text as a term in `[glossary.terms]`, with its aliases, definition, and link. | Text selected in one paragraph or heading |
| Change a feature's availability | Set where a feature in `[features]` is available, such as its state or version. | Anywhere in a page |
| Rename this phrase everywhere | Change a phrase's key in `[phrases]` and every `{key}` that uses it: the one at the cursor, or one you choose. | Anywhere in a page; a phrase at the cursor is the one renamed |
| Rename a dimension value everywhere | Change a value in `[dimensions]` and everywhere it's used: `@variant` attributes, `variant:`, availability, and builds. | Anywhere in a page; a `@variant` attribute's value at the cursor is the one renamed |

Settings:

| Setting | Default | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| `ascribe.path` | `""` | The `ascribe` binary to run, for every project. |
| `ascribe.startServers` | `"onDemand"` | When to start the language server of each `ascribe.toml` project in the workspace. |
| `ascribe.formatOnSave` | `false` | Format Ascribe constructs into canonical form when saving. |
| `ascribe.agents.promptTarget` | `"clipboard"` | Where **Prompt agent** puts the prompt it builds for your agent. |
| `ascribe.preview.scrollPreviewWithEditor` | `true` | Scroll the preview to the block at the top of the editor, and to the block the cursor moves to when it's out of view. |
| `ascribe.preview.scrollEditorWithPreview` | `true` | Scroll the editor to the line of the block at the top of the preview when the preview is scrolled. |
| `ascribe.review.sourceComments` | `"auto"` | Whether the source editor shows the pull request's review threads on the lines they're on, while review is on. |
| `ascribe.maxCrashes` | `5` | How many crashes of a project's language server, since it was last restarted by hand, make the extension stop restarting it and explain why. |
| `ascribe.trace.server` | `"off"` | Log the conversation with the language server to its output channel, for reporting a problem. |

## `@ascribed/astro`

For site builders. Read from `packages/astro/src/index.ts`, `packages/astro/package.json`.

The integration's options:

| Option | Type | Required | What it's for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build` | `string` | In its form | The build whose site output is the collection (a name in `ascribe.toml`). |
| `project` | `string` | No | The directory holding `ascribe.toml`, relative to the Astro root. |
| `projects` | `ProjectEntry[]` | In its form | The projects, each a named build of a project; two entries may share a project. |
| `binary` | `string` | No | The `ascribe` binary, relative to the Astro root. |
| `anchors` | `boolean \| "dev"` | No | Mark each block of the site output with the source lines it came from (source anchors), for review: `"dev"` in `astro dev` only, `true` always. |
| `review` | `boolean \| string` | No | Review in the site preview: an **Ascribe review** app in `astro dev`'s toolbar, which marks the page's changes and shows the pull request's comments, with source anchors in `astro dev`. |
| `codeTitles` | `boolean` | No | Show a code block's title (`title="…"` in its info string, as `@snippet` writes it) above it, with a Shiki transformer that puts the block in a `<figure class="code-title">` with a `<figcaption>`. |

What a site imports:

| Entry | Kind |
|---|---|
| `@ascribed/astro` | An import |
| `@ascribed/astro/rehype` | An import |
| `@ascribed/astro/satteri` | An import |
| `@ascribed/astro/Elements.astro` | An import |

## The outputs

For site builders, and tools. Read from `docs/content/_generated/cli-synopsis.md`, `schemas/`.

A build's outputs, by `--emit`: `site`, `plain`, `json`. Each has a contract under `docs/content/contracts/`.

The JSON the commands and the language server write, each with a schema:

| Schema | Shape | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `schemas/check.schema.json` | CheckReport | What `ascribe check --format json` and `ascribe build --format json` write: one document, whatever the outcome. |
| `schemas/diff-html-data.schema.json` | ReportData | The data the report's script draws from. |
| `schemas/diff.schema.json` | DiffReport | The whole report, as `ascribe diff --format json` writes it. |
| `schemas/drift.schema.json` | DriftReport | The report, as `ascribe drift --format json` writes it. |
| `schemas/explain-list.schema.json` | ExplainListReport | What `ascribe explain --list` answers: every diagnostic. |
| `schemas/explain.schema.json` | ExplainReport | What `ascribe explain <CODE>` answers: one diagnostic. |
| `schemas/fmt.schema.json` | FmtReport | What `ascribe fmt --format json` writes: one document. |
| `schemas/link.schema.json` | LinkReport | What `ascribe link <TARGET> --from <PAGE>` answers. |
| `schemas/lsp-agent-prompt.schema.json` | AgentPromptResult | The answer to `ascribe/agentPrompt`, or `null` when there's nothing to prompt about: the file has no problem, the diagnostic is no longer reported, review is off, or the page or fragment didn't change. |
| `schemas/lsp-build-view.schema.json` | BuildViewResult | The answer to `ascribe/buildView`. |
| `schemas/lsp-changes.schema.json` | ChangesResult | The answer to `ascribe/review/changes`. |
| `schemas/lsp-context.schema.json` | ContextResult | The answer to `ascribe/context`. |
| `schemas/lsp-edit.schema.json` | EditResult | The answer to `ascribe/edit`: the edit, or why there is none. |
| `schemas/lsp-inventory.schema.json` | InventoryResult | The answer to `ascribe/inventory`. |
| `schemas/lsp-preview.schema.json` | PreviewResult | The answer to `ascribe/preview`. |
| `schemas/lsp-set-base.schema.json` | SetBaseResult | The answer to `ascribe/review/setBase`. |
| `schemas/lsp-targets.schema.json` | TargetsResult | The answer to `ascribe/targets`: a list for each kind asked for, and no others. |
| `schemas/model.schema.json` | ModelReport | What `ascribe model --format json` answers: the content model's sections, or the one asked for. |
| `schemas/outline.schema.json` | OutlineReport | What `ascribe outline <PAGE>` answers. |
| `schemas/permalinks-list.schema.json` | PermalinksListReport | What `ascribe permalinks list` answers. |
| `schemas/permalinks-retire.schema.json` | PermalinksRetireReport | What `ascribe permalinks retire` did. |
| `schemas/permalinks-sync.schema.json` | PermalinksSyncReport | What `ascribe permalinks sync` does to the list. |
| `schemas/permalinks-verify.schema.json` | PermalinksVerifyReport | What `ascribe permalinks verify` answers. |
| `schemas/refs.schema.json` | RefsReport | What `ascribe refs <TARGET>` answers. |
| `schemas/render.schema.json` | RenderReport | What `ascribe render <PAGE> --format json` answers. |
| `schemas/report.schema.json` | ReportReport | What `ascribe report --format json` writes: one document, whatever the outcome. |
| `schemas/sources-status.schema.json` | SourcesStatusReport | What `ascribe sources status --format json` writes: each source's pin and the state of its copies, read from the files alone. |
| `schemas/sources-update.schema.json` | SourcesUpdateReport | What `ascribe sources update --format json` writes: how each source's pin moved, and the pages whose examples the new copies change. |

## What nothing declares

These are part of the surface, and no file a script can read lists them, so they're typed in `scripts/surface/inventory.ts`. Each is a surface with no single home.

| Surface | What | Where it lives instead |
|---|---|---|
| The command line | What each command's exit codes mean | The prose of `docs/content/reference/cli.md`, command by command; the three codes are in `crates/ascribe-cli/src/exit.rs` |
| The language | The reserved frontmatter keys: `available`, `variant`, `formatted`, `permalink`, `intended`, and `slug` under the `astro` profile | Checked in `crates/ascribe-model/src/sections.rs`; described in SPEC §2.1 |
| The language | Attributes each directive takes, phrases (`{key}`), and the inline forms | `Builtin::schema` in `crates/ascribe-core/src/schema.rs`, as code, not as a list |
| `ascribe.toml` | Each section's keys | The loader, `crates/ascribe-model/src/`, and the reference's prose |
| The VS Code extension | The status bar item (the build, and review's state), the preview and its header, the build lens, and review's marks and threads | `packages/vscode/src/`, as code |
| What `ascribe agents sync` writes | A block in `AGENTS.md`; the skill in `.agents/skills/ascribe/` and `.claude/skills/ascribe/`; rules in `.claude/rules/ascribe-*.md` and `.github/instructions/ascribe-*.instructions.md`; with `--with-hook`, entries in `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json`, and `.codex/hooks.json`; with `--cloud`, a block in the Copilot setup workflow | `crates/ascribe-cli/src/agents/`, and decisions 53, 58, and 59 |
| Files Ascribe puts in a project | `ascribe.lock`; `ascribe.permalinks`; `sources/`; the output directory, `.ascribe/build/` unless `[project] output-dir` says otherwise; `.ascribe/dev.json` while `astro dev` runs; `.vale.ini` and `.vale/` after `ascribe vale eject` | Each in the crate that writes it |
| `@ascribed/astro` | The dev toolbar's review app, and what the integration serves: published files, `llms.txt`, each page's Markdown, and a page for each permalink | `packages/astro/src/`, as code |
| The outputs | The HTML report `ascribe diff --format html` writes, and the layout of each output's folder | `packages/review/`, and `docs/content/contracts/output-layout.md` |
